name: winotch_notifications
description: Read the notifications every app sent to winotch, newest first: mail, GitHub, your own apps and more. Each has an id, its app, title, body, time (ms), whether it was read, its actions, and `acted`: the action the user pressed, if any.

app.description: Only this app's (its id, as winotch_apps lists it).

unread_only.description: Only what the user has not read.

name: winotch_apps
description: The apps connected to winotch: id, name, sign, and what their pill says now.

name: winotch_notify
description: Show the user a notification in winotch, from Claude Code. Use it for something that needs their eye, or for a draft waiting for their decision: give it actions (for example approve / reject), then read winotch_notifications later; its `acted` field tells which one they pressed. Never treat a draft as approved until `acted` says so.

body.description: A few lines of detail, at most 2000 characters.

importance.description: high opens the island; normal peeks it; low waits behind the bell.

url.description: Opened when the user clicks the notification.

name: winotch_mark_read
description: Mark notifications read: one (id), one app's (app), or all of them (neither).

name: winotch_mail_accounts
description: The Gmail accounts connected to winotch: email, label, status (connecting, ok, error), error and unread count. Use an account's email as `account` in the other mail tools.

name: winotch_mail_search
description: Search the user's Gmail with Gmail's own search syntax (from:ana is:unread newer_than:7d, subject:invoice, has:attachment…), across all mail, not only the inbox. Returns the newest matches: id, thread, account, from, subject, date (ms), unread, snippet, url. Read-only: nothing is marked read.

account.description: One account's email; every account when left out.

query.description: A Gmail search, as typed in Gmail's search box.

name: winotch_mail_read
description: Read one Gmail message in full (or its whole thread): headers (from, to, cc, date, subject, message id), the plain-text body (HTML mail converted to text) and the attachments' names. Read-only: it is not marked read.

id.description: The message's id, as winotch_mail_search returns it.

thread.description: The whole conversation, oldest first (at most its newest 25 mails).

name: winotch_mail_draft
description: Save a draft in the user's Gmail (its Drafts folder) and show it on the winotch island with Send, Open in Gmail and Discard. This NEVER sends: only the user sends, by pressing Send on the island (or from Gmail). Give reply_to to answer a mail: the draft is threaded under it, its subject gets "Re:", and `to` defaults to the original sender. Read winotch_notifications (app gmail) later; `acted` says whether the user sent or discarded it.

account.description: The account it is from (its email).

to.description: Addresses ("Name <a@b.com>" or a@b.com). May be left out when replying.

subject.description: When replying, may be empty: the original's, with "Re:".

reply_to.description: The id of the mail this answers, as winotch_mail_search returns it.

name: winotch_today_list
description: The user's to-dos in winotch's Today app for a range of days (by default today and the 7 days after), plus what is overdue (not done, from before the range) and someday's (no date). Also returns `today` (YYYY-MM-DD), `weekday` and `now` (HH:MM) on the user's clock: use them to turn "tomorrow", "friday" or "in 3 days" into a date yourself before calling winotch_today_add or winotch_today_update. Each to-do: id, title, note, date (YYYY-MM-DD; absent: someday), time (HH:MM, 24 h), done, doneAt and created (ms).

to.description: Last day, YYYY-MM-DD, included (default: 7 days after from).

done.description: Only done (true) or only open (false) to-dos; both when left out.

all.description: Every to-do there is, any day, done or not (from and to are ignored).

name: winotch_today_add
description: Add a to-do to the user's Today; it shows on the island at once. Give `date` as YYYY-MM-DD, worked out from `today` (winotch_today_list) when the user says "tomorrow" or a weekday; leave it out for someday. With `time` (HH:MM, 24 h) the island reminds the user then, with a Done button. A time needs a date.

name: winotch_today_update
description: Change a to-do: rename it, move it to another day or time, change its note, tick it off (done: true) or reopen it (done: false). Only the fields given change; null clears note, date or time (clearing the date clears the time too). Dates YYYY-MM-DD, times HH:MM.

id.description: The to-do's id ("t12"), as winotch_today_list returns it.

time.description: HH:MM, or null for no time (and no reminder).

name: winotch_today_delete
description: Delete a to-do for good, its reminder with it. When it was done, prefer winotch_today_update with done: true.

name: winotch_notes_list
description: The user's notes in winotch's Today app, the one edited last first: id, title, updated (ms), chars and a preview. With `query`, it searches: only the notes whose title or text has every word of it, each with a snippet. Read one whole with winotch_notes_read.

query.description: Words to search for, any case; every one must be in the note.

name: winotch_notes_read
description: Read one note whole: id, title, body (plain text), updated and created (ms).

name: winotch_notes_write
description: Write a note in the user's Today: without `id` a new one; with `id` it replaces that note's title and/or body (only the fields given). Plain text, the body at most 20000 characters. To add to a note without rewriting it, use winotch_notes_append.

id.description: The note to replace; left out: a new note.

title.description: One line, at most 200 characters. A new note without one is titled by its first line.

name: winotch_notes_append
description: Add text at the end of a note, on a new line, leaving what is there as it is.

name: winotch_notes_delete
description: Delete a note for good.

name: winotch_sessions
description: The user's Claude Code sessions on this computer, the newest first: id, folder (the project's folder name), title, cwd, updated (ms since 1970) and whether it is open in a terminal now. With `folder`, only that folder's (its name, any case: "my-app" or "My-App"). Use it to find the one to open: "my last my-app session" is the first one of folder my-app.

folder.description: Only the sessions of this folder (its name).

name: winotch_open_session
description: Open one of the user's Claude Code sessions (its id, from winotch_sessions): in the island's chat (`in`: "chat", the default: the chat shows it, once this answer is done) or its terminal brought to the front (`in`: "terminal"; VS Code on its folder when it has none). Say in a few words what you opened.

id.description: The session's id, as winotch_sessions lists it.

in.description: Where: the island's chat (default) or its terminal.

name: winotch_open_folder
description: Show a folder in File Explorer, by its full path (a session's cwd, for one). Never a file.
